title: Chapter 90 — Running Yourself by Numbers: The Measurement Mindset
intro: The measurement mindset, leading versus lagging indicators, and honest data.

sections.title: Why Measure
sections.content:
You cannot improve what you do not measure. And you cannot manage what you do not track. Most reps have a vague sense of how they are doing — 'I had a good month' or 'It has been slow.' That is feeling, not data.

The rep who knows their close rate is 28 percent can set a goal of 32 percent. The rep who knows their average ticket is $1,800 can focus on step-ups to hit $2,200. The rep who knows their attach rate is 19 percent can make a conscious effort to present warranty and accessories on every sale.

Numbers give you something to work with. Feelings give you something to worry about.

sections.title: Leading vs Lagging
sections.content:
Lagging indicators tell you what already happened: revenue, units sold, total margin. You cannot change last month's revenue. You can only look at it.

Leading indicators tell you what is about to happen: number of ups taken, quotes sent, Daily Five calls made, follow-ups completed, training hours logged. These are the controllable inputs that drive the lagging outputs.

Manage your inputs. Trust the arithmetic. If you take more ups, send more quotes, and follow up more consistently, the revenue follows. Always.

sections.title: Honest Data
sections.content:
Do not game your numbers. Do not count a browser as a qualified up to inflate your close rate. Do not split one sale into two transactions to inflate your unit count. Do not log a voicemail as a completed follow-up.

Honest data is the only useful data. If your close rate is 18 percent and that bothers you, good — fix it. If you pretend it is 28 percent by inflating your denominator, you lose the ability to improve because you cannot see the real problem.
